articleTitle: European and international standards for statements of uncertainty-conceptual background and basic implications
publicationTitle: IEE Workshop on Uncertainties Workshop: Electrical Measurements (Ref. No. 1999/197)
abstract: Starting from the general concept of a measuring process and the naive view of measurement uncertainty, the paper presents the modern GUM view of measurement uncertainty and discusses the interdependence of the standard measurement uncertainty and the expanded measurement uncertainty, the last one being mostly used in trade and industry.

publicationTitle: IEE Workshop on Uncertainties Workshop: Electrical Measurements (Ref. No. 1999/197)
abstract: All measurements are tainted by imperfectly known errors, so the significance associated with the result of a measurement must account for this uncertainty. This paper explores the reasoning behind, and the requirements for, the expression of a value of uncertainty associated with a measurement result.

articleTitle: The importance of uncertainty of measurement
publicationTitle: IEE Workshop on Uncertainties Workshop: Electrical Measurements (Ref. No. 1999/197)
abstract: Much progress has been made in the last 30 years in the promotion of the importance of uncertainty of measurement being quoted with all calibration results and the authors of the many guidance documents on the subject must be given considerable credit for this achievement. However it is essential that their efforts are not wasted and a vigorous campaign must be maintained until all certificates of calibration contain uncertainties of measurement. Without such information calibration results have no value.

articleTitle: Pro-forma worked examples on uncertainty in electrical measurement
publicationTitle: IEE Workshop on Uncertainties Workshop: Electrical Measurements (Ref. No. 1999/197)
abstract: Most measurements made in the electrical field will be subject to errors of some kind, however small. A measured value should therefore be stated with a corresponding measurement uncertainty to define the probable limits of variation in the result. This paper is aimed at describing the logic and use of pro-forma methods for the calculation of formal uncertainty budgets for the more common instrument based measurement facilities, such as calibrators and DMMs, albeit the technique may be applied to most measurement situations.

articleTitle: Relating measurement uncertainties to manufacturers specifications
publicationTitle: IEE Workshop on Uncertainties Workshop: Electrical Measurements (Ref. No. 1999/197)
abstract: Many products submitted for calibration do not need to meet any particular requirement but the user still requires that the product is satisfactorily and adequately calibrated. In many cases, the user of the product is not aware of his precise calibration needs and normally requests calibration to the manufacturers specification. The calibration laboratory will need to determine precisely what tests need to be performed to satisfy the request. Relating manufacturers product specifications to the measurement standards and measurement uncertainties is therefore an important function of the calibration laboratory to ensure that adequate calibration is carried out.
